chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about passing through Medina during the outbound journey (al-badaya), is it better, or during the return journey (al-rija'a)? He said: There is no harm with that, whichever it is.
ai.seo_question: Is it better to visit Medina before or after Haj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Although the chapter title in *Al-Istibsar* suggests a preference for visiting Medina during the initial journey (al-badaya) for those coming via Iraq, this specific narration from Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that there is no strict obligation or harm in visiting during either the outbound or return leg. This highlights the flexibility (rukhsa) in Shia jurisprudence regarding the timing of ziyarah, prioritizing the spiritual benefit over rigid chronological constraints. The ruling underscores that while certain times may be recommended for greater reward, the validity and acceptability of the visit remain intact regardless of the journey's phase.
